questions.stem:
Statements: A > B > C
Conclusions:
I. A > C
II. B > A
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: A > B > C
Conclusion I (A > C): A > B and B > C → A > C ✓
Conclusion II (B > A): Chain gives A > B, so B > A is false ✗
Only Conclusion I follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: P = Q > R
Conclusions:
I. Q = R
II. P > R
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: P = Q > R
Conclusion I (Q = R): Q > R means Q ≠ R ✗
Conclusion II (P > R): P = Q > R → P > R ✓
Only Conclusion II follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: X < Y ≤ Z
Conclusions:
I. X < Z
II. Y = Z
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: X < Y ≤ Z
Conclusion I (X < Z): X < Y and Y ≤ Z → X < Z ✓
Conclusion II (Y = Z): Y ≤ Z; Y could be strictly less than Z, so Y = Z is not guaranteed ✗
Only Conclusion I follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: M ≥ N = O
Conclusions:
I. M ≥ O
II. N > M
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: M ≥ N = O
Conclusion I (M ≥ O): M ≥ N and N = O → M ≥ O ✓
Conclusion II (N > M): M ≥ N means M is at least N, so N > M is false ✗
Only Conclusion I follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: A ≤ B = C
Conclusions:
I. A < C
II. A ≤ C
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: A ≤ B = C
Conclusion I (A < C): A ≤ B = C → A ≤ C; strict A < C requires A < B, which is not guaranteed (A could equal B = C) ✗
Conclusion II (A ≤ C): A ≤ B = C → A ≤ C always holds ✓
Only Conclusion II follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements:
1. P > Q
2. Q < R
Conclusions:
I. P > R
II. P = R
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Given: P > Q and Q < R — both P and R are greater than Q, but their mutual relationship is unknown.
Example 1: P=5, Q=2, R=3 → P > R (I true, II false)
Example 2: P=3, Q=2, R=5 → P < R (I false, II false)
Example 3: P=4, Q=2, R=4 → P = R (II true, I false)
Neither conclusion necessarily follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: X > Y ≥ Z
Conclusions:
I. X ≥ Z
II. X > Z
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: X > Y ≥ Z
X > Y (strict) and Y ≥ Z → X > Z (strict) ✓
Since X > Z (strict), X ≥ Z is also true ✓
Both Conclusions I and II follow.
Key rule: a strict inequality X > Z implies the non-strict X ≥ Z as well.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: A > B ≥ C > D
Conclusions:
I. A > D
II. B > D
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: A > B ≥ C > D
Conclusion I (A > D): A > B ≥ C > D → A > D ✓
Conclusion II (B > D): B ≥ C > D → B > D ✓
Both Conclusions I and II follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: P < Q > R ≤ S
Conclusions:
I. P < S
II. Q > S
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Given: P < Q, Q > R, R ≤ S
Conclusion I (P < S): No direct P-to-S link. Counterexample: P=4, Q=5, R=3, S=3.5 → P(4) > S(3.5) ✗
Conclusion II (Q > S): Q > R ≤ S — S could be much larger. Counterexample: Q=5, R=3, S=8 → Q < S ✗
Neither conclusion necessarily follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: M ≥ N > O = P
Conclusions:
I. N = P
II. M > P
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: M ≥ N > O = P
Conclusion I (N = P): N > O = P → N > P, so N ≠ P ✗
Conclusion II (M > P): M ≥ N > O = P → M > P ✓
Only Conclusion II follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: X > Y ≤ Z < W
Conclusions:
I. X > Z
II. Y < W
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Given: X > Y, Y ≤ Z, Z < W
Conclusion I (X > Z): X > Y ≤ Z — X could be less than Z. Counterexample: X=3, Y=2, Z=10 → X < Z ✗
Conclusion II (Y < W): Y ≤ Z and Z < W → Y ≤ Z < W → Y < W ✓
Only Conclusion II follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: A = B ≥ C > D
Conclusions:
I. A > D
II. B = C
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: A = B ≥ C > D
Conclusion I (A > D): A = B ≥ C > D → A ≥ C > D → A > D ✓
Conclusion II (B = C): B ≥ C; B could be strictly greater than C, so B = C is not guaranteed ✗
Only Conclusion I follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: P > Q ≥ R = S
Conclusions:
I. P > S
II. Q > S
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: P > Q ≥ R = S
Conclusion I (P > S): P > Q ≥ R = S → P > S ✓
Conclusion II (Q > S): Q ≥ R = S → Q ≥ S; when Q = R = S, then Q = S, so Q > S fails ✗
Only Conclusion I follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements:
1. M < N
2. O = N > P
Conclusions:
I. M > P
II. P > M
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Combined: M < N = O > P — both M and P are less than N, but their mutual relationship is unknown.
Example 1: M=4, N=5, P=3 → M > P (I true, II false)
Example 2: M=2, N=5, P=4 → P > M (II true, I false)
Neither conclusion necessarily follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: X ≥ Y > Z ≤ W
Conclusions:
I. X > Z
II. Y < W
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: X ≥ Y > Z ≤ W
Conclusion I (X > Z): X ≥ Y > Z → X > Z (since Y > Z strict) ✓
Conclusion II (Y < W): Y > Z ≤ W — Counterexample: Y=5, Z=3, W=4 → Y(5) > W(4) ✗
Only Conclusion I follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: A > B = C ≤ D
Conclusions:
I. A > C
II. B ≤ D
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: A > B = C ≤ D
Conclusion I (A > C): A > B = C → A > C ✓
Conclusion II (B ≤ D): B = C ≤ D → B ≤ D ✓
Both Conclusions I and II follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: P ≥ Q > R > S
Conclusions:
I. P > S
II. Q ≥ S
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: P ≥ Q > R > S
Conclusion I (P > S): P ≥ Q > R > S → P > S ✓
Conclusion II (Q ≥ S): Q > R > S → Q > S, which implies Q ≥ S ✓
Both Conclusions I and II follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: X < Y ≤ Z > W
Conclusions:
I. X < Z
II. W < Y
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: X < Y ≤ Z > W
Conclusion I (X < Z): X < Y ≤ Z → X < Z ✓
Conclusion II (W < Y): Z > W but Y ≤ Z. Counterexample: Y=3, Z=5, W=4 → W(4) > Y(3) ✗
Only Conclusion I follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: M > N ≥ O ≥ P
Conclusions:
I. M > P
II. N = O
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: M > N ≥ O ≥ P
Conclusion I (M > P): M > N ≥ O ≥ P → M > P ✓
Conclusion II (N = O): N ≥ O; N could be strictly greater than O, so N = O is not guaranteed ✗
Only Conclusion I follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: A ≥ B > C = D ≤ E
Conclusions:
I. A > D
II. B ≤ E
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: A ≥ B > C = D ≤ E
Conclusion I (A > D): A ≥ B > C = D → A > D ✓
Conclusion II (B ≤ E): B > D and D ≤ E, but B > D ≤ E does not fix B vs E. Counterexample: B=5, D=3, E=4 → B(5) > E(4) ✗
Only Conclusion I follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: P < Q = R ≥ S > T
Conclusions:
I. P < R
II. S > T
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: P < Q = R ≥ S > T
Conclusion I (P < R): P < Q = R → P < R ✓
Conclusion II (S > T): S > T is directly present in the chain ✓
Both Conclusions I and II follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements:
1. X > Y ≥ Z
2. Z < W ≤ V
Conclusions:
I. X > Z
II. Y < V
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
From Statement 1: X > Y ≥ Z → X > Z ✓ (Conclusion I holds)
Conclusion II (Y < V): Y ≥ Z and Z < W ≤ V gives Z < V; but Y ≥ Z and Z < V does not force Y < V. Counterexample: Y=5, Z=3, W=4, V=4 → Y(5) > V(4) ✗
Only Conclusion I follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: M = N > O > P ≥ Q
Conclusions:
I. M > Q
II. N > P
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: M = N > O > P ≥ Q
Conclusion I (M > Q): M = N > O > P ≥ Q → M > Q ✓
Conclusion II (N > P): N = M > O > P → N > P ✓
Both Conclusions I and II follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: A ≤ B < C = D > E
Conclusions:
I. A < D
II. B > E
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: A ≤ B < C = D > E
Conclusion I (A < D): A ≤ B < C = D → A < D ✓
Conclusion II (B > E): B < C = D > E — D > E but B < D; B vs E is unknown. Counterexample: B=3, D=5, E=4 → B(3) < E(4) ✗
Only Conclusion I follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements:
1. P > Q ≥ R
2. R = S < T
Conclusions:
I. P > S
II. Q ≥ S
Which conclusion(s) definitely follow?
questions.explanation:
Combining both statements: P > Q ≥ R = S < T
Conclusion I (P > S): P > Q ≥ R = S → P > S ✓
Conclusion II (Q ≥ S): Q ≥ R = S → Q ≥ S ✓
Both Conclusions I and II follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning
